A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOCHA and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original personalized-detection experiments on four datasets, component ablations, PCA studies, qualitative results, and Wilcoxon tests.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds student-architecture experiments, few-shot-classifier ablations, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The overall pipeline, translator, PCA targets, and combined objective remain. Section 3.4 revises the specified relational-loss formulation: Eq. (7) replaces temperature-scaled Euclidean distances with normalized distances, explicitly excludes diagonal entries before softmax, and removes the explicit temperature. This establishes a limited formulation revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO and OpenImages for pretraining/distillation and PerSeg, POD, CORe50, and iCubWorld for personalization. The added architecture, classifier, and efficiency experiments do not introduce different datasets, task requirements, or input environments.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same teacher and comparison-method sets, including AuXFT, ViLD, KL divergence, KL plus MSE, and OFA. The new ablations vary student architectures and downstream classifiers while retaining undistilled, AuXFT, and MOCHA supervision comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 substantially expands evaluation configurations through YOLOv11n/s/l and RT-DETR-l students, alternative ProtoNet, SimpleShot, and linear-probing classifiers, and computational-cost measurements (Tables 3 and 6–8). Existing task metrics, few-shot regimes, and 50/20-epoch distillation budgets remain. The expanded retrieval-protocol explanation documents existing experiments rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: v4 adds systematic analyses of dependence on student family and size, downstream few-shot classifier, and computational overhead. These test architectural generality, representation robustness, and efficiency beyond v1's component studies. The earlier PCA, loss, translator, initialization, learning-rate, toy, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report variability alongside scores and the same Wilcoxon comparisons and p-values (v1 Table A.4; v4 Table 5). No new seed counts, repetition counts, confidence intervals, or statistical-testing procedures are documented. Additional result rows and timing variability extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark, component-ablation, PCA, and Wilcoxon table values are unchanged. v4 adds substantial architecture, classifier, and efficiency results; for example, Table 3 reports RT-DETR-l PerSeg scores of 43.5 without distillation, 45.2 with AuXFT, and 47.0 with MOCHA. Appendix A.4 revises reported 50/20-epoch training times from 48/20 hours to 28/11 hours. These are added results and revised timing reports, not improved scores in the retained comparisons.

T1.justification: Eq. (7) revises the mathematical definition of relational affinities through distance normalization, explicit diagonal exclusion, and removal of temperature. v4 Table 6 also introduces asymptotic distillation-cost expressions. The remaining loss equations and PCA fitting formulation are retained; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: v4 drops the abstract's claim that MOCHA performs on par with larger multimodal models. The central object-level multimodal-distillation contribution, personalized-detection application, and +10.1 average improvement claim remain. Its conclusion emphasizes tested student architectures, supporting the existing architecture-agnostic framing.

C2.justification: v4 explains the oracle-versus-detection retrieval gap using single versus multiple candidate boxes, interprets smaller gains on larger or different students through capacity and architectural mismatch, and attributes training efficiency to embedding caching. It also interprets classifier ablations as evidence of representation robustness. The existing detection-only, training-cost, and prototype-scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 provides a project-repository URL and requirements.txt pointer, documents deterministic augmentation and teacher-embedding caching, adds parameter counts and linear-probing settings, and clarifies retrieval evaluation. It also revises training-time estimates while retaining the hardware and epoch disclosures. These materially expand reproducibility information; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for YOLO11, RT-DETRv2, and SimpleShot and removes the Deeply-Supervised Nets and Going Deeper with Convolutions references. Related work newly identifies AuXFT as the only prior work with a similar setup and sharpens distinctions from prompt-driven recognition. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites the abstract and conclusion, revises introductory and results explanations, and substantially reorganizes the appendix into performance evaluation, additional ablations, implementation, qualitative results, and limitations. References move after the appendix, citations become numeric, and several unresolved cross-references are repaired.

P2.justification: v4 adds architecture, computational-cost, and classifier tables, while some rows repeat existing comparisons. It extensively restyles tables, captions, headings, and pseudocode, including smaller gray uncertainty values and colored algorithm comments. Existing figures are retained with resizing, relabeling, and relocation; the PCA and qualitative appendix displays change order.

improvement.justification: v1's architectural-generality and deployment-efficiency claims had limited direct validation. v4 substantially strengthens them through additional detector families, classifier ablations, and explicit latency, memory, and training-cost comparisons, while improving reproducibility and explaining the otherwise puzzling retrieval-score differences. Some new interpretation overreaches: Table 7 reports YOLOv11l CORe50 5-shot accuracy of 61.0 for MOCHA versus 63.5 for AuXFT despite claiming superiority across all settings. This qualification does not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and transparency.
